pr_title: Allow Humidifier.current_humidity to be a float
pr_body:
## Proposed change
To enable strict typing for the `generic_hygrostat` integration, https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/107272 changed the value for `current_humidity` from `float | None` to `int | None` as it's defined in the base class.

As mentioned in #111295, there are cases / sensors which report with greater precision so artificially limiting us to integers doesn't make much sense.

_If required, I can open an architecture discussion for it. However as it just restores the behavior prior to `2024.2.0` and is quite small, I haven't done so yet._

> Please adjust the type annotation of `current_humitidy` of all the humidifier platforms and also the humidifier entity attributes `_attr_current_humidity`, max/min humidity, target humidity etc. All humidity values should be floats to make it consistent.

I'm fine to do that, just the question if it's necessary to adjust other platforms too. For subtyping rules it's enough to modify the base humidifier entity. All other platforms are fine to define a narrower type. That's also how we do it in other cases. E.g. `native_value` for `SensorEntity` has a broad return type of `StateType | date | datetime | Decimal`. In contrast platforms frequently choose only a narrower ones like `str | None`, `int` or other.

Regarding `max/min`, `target` humidity. I can do that too. However, that it make sense? I think those are values set as targets for humidifiers. Don't know if anyone allows users to target a float value if the precision isn't high enough in the first place. Who sets there AC to target `45.7 %` humidity after all?

**Edit**
`current_humidity` is different as it's a sensor reading.

If the sensor can measure floats the actuator may be able accept floats as target.

It also makes sense to have it consistent just from a developer perspective.
It's ok to keep platforms typed as int if that's what they're using natively.
@cdce8p Did you check how this looks like in the UI when a floats are assigned?

Ok. So I've updated `current_humidity`, `target_humidity`, `min_humidity` and `max_humidity` now, for both `humidifier` and `climate` entities. Aside from restoring the behavior of `generic_hygrostat` and changing two demo entities, this PR doesn't change the behavior of existing integrations. I thought about updating the `set_humidity` methods as well. However, I don't think it's possible to do that in a backwards compatible manner., unfortunately As soon as we change the `vol.Coerce` from `int` to `float` (custom) integrations which expect integers for `humidity` could start to fail. > Did you check how this looks like in the UI when a floats are assigned? Yes. At least the default cards for `climate` and `humidifer` can handle a `float` value for `current_humidity` already. See screenshots below. `target_humidity` is assumed to be `int`. Not sure it makes sense to update that though since we can't update `set_humidity` itself (see above). If uses can't set float values through service calls there isn't really a need to be able to display them in the frontend. _I decided to leave `target_humidity` as `float` only for consistency._ -- Also opened a PR to update the dev documentation: https://github.com/home-assistant/developers.home-assistant/pull/2121

issue_context.title: generic_hygrostat chart noisy after current_humidity typing change to an int
issue_context.body: ### The problem Starting with HA 2024.2.0, the dashboard chart for generic_hygrostat started looking less than pleasing because the internal current_humidity property changed from a non-defined type (float) to an int. Instead of 2 decimals of accuracy and a smooth chart on my install, it now displays as a noisy integer. Was this a conscious decision, and is the author open to changing current_humidity to a float to restore the prior functionality? The sensor I use is accurate to +/- 1% and would benefit from a decimal or two. Thanks for your hard work! Author: @cdce8p, commit: 5ae4193, PR: #107272 Example chart; the left side is the old/float view, the right side is the new/int view. ### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue? core-2024.2.3 ### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core? 2024.1.x ### What type of installation are you running? Home Assistant OS ### Integration causing the issue generic_hygrostat ### Link to integration documentation on our website https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/generic_hygrostat/ ### Diagnostics information _No response_ ### Example YAML snippet ```yaml - platform: generic_hygrostat name: Humidifier device_class: humidifier humidifier: switch.humidifier_relay target_sensor: sensor.main_floor_relative_humidity_safe min_humidity: 15 max_humidity: 45 target_humidity: 25 dry_tolerance: 2 wet_tolerance: 1 sensor_stale_duration: 00:15:00 # turns off if humidity reading is unavailable keep_alive: 00:05:00 # refreshes state initial_state: False main_floor_relative_humidity_safe: friendly_name: Humidity unit_of_measurement: "%" value_template: >- {% set invalid_value = -48 %} {% set result = states('sensor.main_floor_relative_humidity') | float(invalid_value) %} {% if result != invalid_value %} {{ result }} {% else %} {{ states("sensor.main_floor_relative_humidity_safe") }} {% endif %} ``` ### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us? _No response_ ### Additional information _No response_

Thanks for opening the issue! Yeah, changing the `current_humidity` value from float to int was a functional change in https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/107272. Reason being that the base class requires it to be `int | None`.

I would be open to adjusting it so that `float` is accepted.
Opened #111297 to revert it and change the `humidifier` base to "officially" allow for `float` values.

review_comments:
The current humidity is documented as an optional integer.

https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/humidifier#properties

The issue says the sensor is accurate to +/- 1 %. Does that mean it isn't actually more accurate than an integer would represent?

Would a home user realistically be interested in and have a sensor that can meaure less than a percent of accuracy of humidity? That sounds far fetched.

> The issue says the sensor is accurate to +/- 1 %. Does that mean it isn't actually more accurate than an integer would represent?
> 
> Would a home user realistically be interested in and have a sensor that can meaure less than a percent of accuracy of humidity? That sounds far fetched.

Not quite. Even if a sensor spec is +/- 1% that doesn't necessarily mean its accuracy isn't higher. Might just have a built in tolerance of up to 1% in each direction.

The main thing to consider though is that we don't do any kind of smoothing when converting the values from float to int. That's why the graph looks a lot more fragmented after the update. Of course it would be possible to apply that afterwards but due to the initial loose of accuracy, you would now be looking more at something like +/- 2%.

/CC @kkalitowski

> The current humidity is documented as an optional integer.
>
> https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/humidifier#properties

I can update that once we decide this change is fine.
I still don't see the need or interest for higher accuracy. It sounds like it's just a problem with how the graph looks, not an actual desire to measure more accurate.

I appreciate the dialog and constructive thoughts. Here is why I think a higher resolution than int would be beneficial:

1. With integer resolution, the chart is difficult to read and trends are hard to see. If the sensor reads 32.48, 32.52, 32.48, the chart bounces from 32-33-32.
2. I have the wet_tolerance on the humidifier set to 1 because I do not want to overdo humidity and have it too high when night comes (it takes a long time to come down). With integer resolution, these tolerances take on a different meaning. A tolerance of 1% now becomes 0.5% due to rounding.
3. Take items 1 and 2 together, and you find that the humdifier might be going on/off every minute, putting wear on the physical components (relay, solenoid, jiggling pipes) and causing extra noise in the house from the pipes. I could compensate with generic_hygrostat's min_cycle_duration, but that strikes me as a workaround, not the real answer to the problem.
You can increase the tolerance to 2 and avoid the problem. Since your sensor isn't more accurate than 1 % it sounds appropriate to set a higher tolerance than 1.

The [Sensiron SHT45](https://sensirion.com/media/documents/33FD6951/6555C40E/Sensirion_Datasheet_SHT4x.pdf) sensor has an accuracy of +/- 1.0% RH, a resolution of 0.01% RH, and repeatability of 0.08% RH.

Yes, it _could_ be off by 1% in either direction depending on the environment or manufacturing issues, but it is mostly consistent and precise in the measurement it provides. It won't return three readings of 30, 29, 31; it will give three readings within 0.08% of each other.

Personally, I think it should be up to the user to decide how precise of a value to send to `current_humidity` instead of being artificially limited to `int`. For one, it makes the chart much more readable so I can have one humidifier chart on the dashboard instead of needing a second chart to also see the more precise data.

But beyond the chart, the rounding adversely affects the functionality and understandability of the humidifier.  With a `dry_tolerance` and `wet_tolerance` each of 1, you are only getting a _total_ range of 1. That’s confusing and narrow. If you bump tolerance to 2, you are getting a range of 3. On the other hand, the cases that use `float` make natural sense and have no chance of causing confusion. Anyone with a sensor resolution better than an integer, which I expect is at least everyone using ESPHome, will have this problem.

Target RH% | Numeric | Wet/dry Tolerance | Real range | Humidifier turns on | Humidifier turns off
---------- | ------------ | --------- | ---------- | ------------------- | --------------------
30         | int          | 1 / 1         | 1.01       | 29.49               | 30.5                
30         | int          | 2 / 2         | 3.01       | 28.49               | 31.5                
30         | float        | 1 / 1         | 2          | 29                  | 31                  
30         | float        | 2 / 2         | 4          | 28                  | 32                  

<I retract my item 3 from my earlier reply; I don't think using `int` is going to cause major problems with a humidifier cycling, though it will still increase cycling because of the rounding>

We've discussed this in the core team and concluded it's ok to change the type to float.

Side note: We think there should be a way for humidifer entities to say what the default precision shown to the user is, similar to how sensor entities have a `suggested_precision` attribute.
